# ng-magic-test-bed
> Streamlined Angular unit test setup utility. Replaces verbose `TestBed.configureTestingModule` boilerplate with a fluent, type-safe API. Uses Jasmine spies automatically. Automatically extends all mocks with all methods of the class to be mocked.
Docs: https://peejay-solutions.github.io/ng-magic-test-bed/
## Installation
```bash
npm install @peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed --save-dev
```
## Core Usage Pattern
```typescript
import { NgMagicSetupTestBed } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
describe('MyService', () => {
  function setup() {
    const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
    const dependencyServiceMock = magic.serviceMock(DependencyService);
    const service = magic.injection(MyService);
    return { service, dependencyServiceMock };
  }
  it('should do X when Y', () => {
    const { service, dependencyServiceMock } = setup();
    dependencyServiceMock.someMethod.and.returnValue('value');
    expect(service.doSomething()).toBe('expected');
  });
});
```
`magic.injection()` triggers TestBed configuration — call it after all mocks are set up.
---
## Choosing the Right Method
Before reading the full API, use this decision tree to pick the correct mock method:
| Situation | Method | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Class is `@Injectable` and registered in DI | `serviceMock(Class, mock?)` | Registers mock in TestBed as provider |
| Class is created by a factory via `new` (not in DI) | `objectMock(Class, mock)` | Creates mock without TestBed registration; auto-spies from prototype |
| Need to mock a TypeScript `interface` (no class/prototype exists) | `interfaceMock<I>(mock)` | Same as `objectMock(undefined, mock)`, but typed as `I` so you don't have to cast |
| Factory class with `create()` method | `factoryMock(FactoryClass, [instances])` | Registers factory in DI; `create()` returns instances sequentially |
| Provider registered via injection token | `providerMock(token, mock)` | Registers mock for a non-class token |
| Service provided at component level | `componentServiceMock(CompClass, SvcClass, mock?)` | Overrides component-level provider |
| Need to assert observable emissions | `observer(observable$)` | Subscribes and tracks all emissions with spies |
| Need the real service instance from DI | `injection(Class)` | Resolves from TestBed; triggers configuration |
---
## NgMagicSetupTestBed API
### Module Setup (call before injection)
| Method | Description |
|---|---|
| `declaration(c)` / `declarations(cs)` | Add component/directive/pipe to declarations |
| `import(m)` / `imports(ms)` | Add module to imports |
| `provider(p)` / `providers(ps)` | Add provider |
| `schema(s)` / `schemas(ss)` | Add schema (`NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` included by default) |
| `keptPipe(c)` | Keep a single pipe as its REAL implementation |
| `keptDirectives(c)` | Keep a directive as its REAL implementation, returns rendered instances |
| `keptComponents(c)` | Keep a child component as its REAL implementation, returns rendered instances |
| `keptComponentImports(cs)` | Keep several pipes/directives/standalone components as their REAL implementation, in one call |
### Keeping template dependencies real
**`keptPipe<C>(pipeClass)`**
Keeps a single pipe as its real implementation (not spied) - it gets added to the fixture component's imports and runs its actual `transform()` logic. Use this when you want to assert on rendered output rather than on whether the pipe was called.
```typescript
magic.keptPipe(CurrencyPipe);
const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent);
expect(fixture.nativeElement.textContent).toContain('$42.00'); // the real pipe ran
```
**`keptDirectives<C>(directiveClass): Array<C>`**
Keeps a directive as its real implementation and returns an array of every instance found in the fixture (usable only after `fixture()` is called - before that it's a placeholder array). Useful when you want the directive's real behavior but still want to inspect its inputs/state on the rendered instance(s).
```typescript
const tooltipDirectives = magic.keptDirectives(TooltipDirective);
const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent);
expect(tooltipDirectives[0].text).toBe('Hello');
```
**`keptComponents<C>(componentClass): Array<C>`**
Same as `keptDirectives()`, but for a child component: keeps its real implementation (real template, real logic) and returns every rendered instance found in the fixture.
```typescript
const cards = magic.keptComponents(CardComponent);
const fixture = magic.fixture(MyListComponent);
expect(cards.length).toBe(3);
```
**`keptComponentImports(cs: Array<Type<any>>)`**
`fixture()` always replaces a standalone root component's `imports` array with only what was explicitly registered through this test bed. Any structural directive or pipe the template relies on (`NgIf`, `NgFor`, `AsyncPipe`, ...) that you don't explicitly keep will silently stop working — no error, the content driven by it just never renders. `keptComponentImports()` keeps several of them as their real implementation in one call, instead of registering each one individually.
```typescript
// Template: <span *ngIf="value$ | async as value">{{ value }}</span>
const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
magic.keptComponentImports([NgIf, AsyncPipe]);
const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent);
// without the line above, *ngIf's content would never render, even
// though MyComponent's own template correctly imports NgIf/AsyncPipe
```
### Mocking
**`serviceMock<S>(serviceClass, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Creates and registers a mock for a service. All methods from serviceClass prototype are auto-spied on the mock. Returns `jasmine.SpyObj<S> & M` — a spy object with all prototype methods as spies, plus your mock properties.
```typescript
// Auto-generated spy mock (no custom mock needed)
const myServiceMock = magic.serviceMock(MyService);
myServiceMock.getData.and.returnValue(of([]));
// Custom partial mock (methods are still wrapped in spies)
const myServiceMock = magic.serviceMock(MyService, new MyServiceMock());
```
**`providerMock<M>(token, mock, dontSpy?, spySource?)`**
Mocks an injection token.
**`providerFunctionMock<F>(token, callback?)`**
Replaces a function provided with an Angular provider token with a spy. An optional `callback` parameter defines default behavior for the mocked provider function. Returns `Spy<F>` on the mocked provider function.
```typescript
const myFunctionMock = magic.providerFunctionMock(MY_FUNCTION_TOKEN, () => {}); 
expect(myFunctionMock).toHaveBeenCalled();
```
**`objectMock<O>(objectClass, mock, dontSpy?)`**
Creates a mock object **without** TestBed registration. Use this for instances that are not in the DI container — typically objects created by factories. All methods from objectClass prototype are auto-spied. Returns `jasmine.SpyObj<O> & M`.
```typescript
const widgetMock = magic.objectMock(Widget, {
    id: 'mock-id',
    dataSource: { itemCreated: null } as any
});
// widgetMock has spies for ALL Widget prototype methods
// plus the properties you provided
```
**`interfaceMock<I>(mock, dontSpy?)`**
Creates a mock object typed as `I & jasmine.SpyObj<I>` for a plain TypeScript **interface** — no class, no prototype, nothing to auto-spy from. `objectMock(undefined, mock)` does the same thing at runtime, but its return type is only `jasmine.SpyObj<M>` (the shape of `mock`, not the interface), so you'd have to cast it to `I` yourself. `interfaceMock` skips that cast. Because interfaces don't exist at runtime, `mock` must implement **every** member of `I` (not `Partial<I>`) — there is no way to auto-generate a spy for a member you didn't provide, so the compiler enforces completeness instead.
```typescript
interface Logger {
    info(message: string): void;
    warn(message: string): void;
}
const loggerMock = magic.interfaceMock<Logger>({
    info: () => {},
    warn: () => {},
});
// loggerMock.info / .warn are both spies, no cast needed
```
**`factoryMock<I, F>(factoryClass, instances)`**
Mocks a factory service in TestBed. The `create()` method returns sequential instances from the provided array. Returns `jasmine.SpyObj<Partial<F>>` — **use this return value directly**, do not fetch the factory via `injection()`.
```typescript
const instance1 = { value: 'a' };
const instance2 = { value: 'b' };
magic.factoryMock(MyFactory, [instance1, instance2]);
// first call to factory.create() returns instance1, second returns instance2
// For instance mocks:
const instanceMock = magic.objectMock(MyApp, { id: 'test' });
const factoryMock = magic.factoryMock(MyAppFactory, [instanceMock]);
// factoryMock.create is a jasmine.Spy — use .calls to inspect:
const callArgs = factoryMock.create.calls.mostRecent().args[0];
```
**`componentServiceMock<S>(componentClass, serviceClass, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks a service provided at the component level (not root).
**`directiveServiceMock<S>(directiveClass, serviceClass, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks a service provided at the directive level.
**`componentProviderMock<M>(componentClass, token, mock, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks an injection token provided by a specific component.
**`directiveProviderMock<M>(directiveClass, token, mock, dontSpy?)`**
Mocks an injection token provided by a specific directive.
### Injection & Fixtures
**`injection<S>(token)`**
Resolves a service/class from DI. Triggers TestBed compilation — call after all mocks are registered. Returns the real service type `S`.
Note: For factories mocked via `factoryMock()`, use the `factoryMock` return value (which is already a `SpyObj`) instead of calling `injection()`.
```typescript
const service = magic.injection(MyService);
```
**`fixture<C>(componentClass, initialInputs?, disableNoErrorSchema?)`**
Creates a `ComponentFixture<C>`. **May only be called once per `NgMagicSetupTestBed` instance.**
- `initialInputs` — an object whose properties are applied via `componentRef.setInput()` **before** the first `detectChanges()`. This is the correct way to set `@Input()` values that are required in `ngOnInit`. Works for both classic `@Input()`-decorated properties and signal-based `input()` properties — for a signal input with a `transform`, pass the transform's input type (the same value a template binding would pass); it gets transformed the same way a real binding would.
- `disableNoErrorSchema` — by default `NO_ERRORS_SCHEMA` is added so unknown child elements/inputs are silently ignored. Pass `true` to disable this and get strict template checking.
- Returns a standard Angular `ComponentFixture<C>` (same as `TestBed.createComponent()`).
- Call after all mocks and `componentMocks`/`directiveMocks` are registered.
```typescript
// Basic fixture with initial inputs - works for @Input() label/count and for
// signal inputs label = input('') / count = input(0) alike
const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent, { label: 'test', count: 42 });
expect(fixture.componentInstance.label).toBe('test'); // or .label() for a signal input
// Full component test pattern
function setup() {
  const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
  const childMocks = magic.componentMocks(MyChildComponentMock);
  const serviceMock = magic.componentServiceMock(MyComponent, MyService, new MyServiceMock());
  const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent, { param: 100 });
  return { fixture, childMocks, serviceMock };
}
it('should render with input', () => {
  const { fixture, serviceMock } = setup();
  expect(fixture.componentInstance.param).toBe(100);
  expect(serviceMock.load).toHaveBeenCalled();
});
```
**`componentMocks<C>(componentClass)`**
Reads inputs and outputs of `componentClass` and registeres a mock component in imports or declarations and returns an array that will be populated with all rendered mock instances **after** `fixture()` is called. Must be called before `fixture()`.
```typescript
// Define a mock component matching the selector you want to stub
@Component({ selector: 'lib-button', template: '' })
class MyButtonMock implements Partial<MyButtonComponent> {
  @Output() click = new EventEmitter();
}
function setup() {
  const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
  const buttons = magic.componentMocks(MyButtonMock);  // call before fixture
  const fixture = magic.fixture(ParentComponent, { param: 100 });
  const firstButton = buttons[0];                      // usable after fixture
  return { fixture, firstButton };
}
it('should react to child click', () => {
  const { firstButton, fixture } = setup();
  firstButton.click.emit();
  fixture.detectChanges();
  // assert parent reaction
});
```
**`directiveMocks<C>(directiveClass)`**
Returns all rendered directive instances after fixture creation. Same call-before-fixture pattern as `componentMocks`.
**`run<T>(fn)`**
Executes a factory function within Angular's injection context. Use this to instantiate classes that call `inject()` in their constructor or field initializers.
```typescript
class MyObject {
  private service = inject(MyService);  // requires injection context
  getValue() { return this.service.getValue(); }
}
it('should support inject()-based classes', () => {
  const magic = new NgMagicSetupTestBed();
  const serviceMock = magic.serviceMock(MyService);
  serviceMock.getValue.and.returnValue(42);
  const obj = magic.run(() => new MyObject());
  expect(obj.getValue()).toBe(42);
});
```
### Observables
**`observer<T>(observable$, name?)`**
Subscribes to an observable and returns a `SpyObserver<T>` for asserting emissions.
```typescript
const events$ = magic.observer(service.events$);
// trigger something
expect(events$.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ type: 'update' });
expect(events$.observations).toEqual([{ type: 'update' }]);
expect(events$.latest).toEqual({ type: 'update' });
```
**`outputObserver<T>(output, name?)`**
Same as `observer()`, but for Angular's signal-based `output()` API (`OutputEmitterRef<T>`) instead of a plain Observable. Use this for a component's `output<T>()`-declared emitters — the counterpart to `observer()` for the older `@Output() = new EventEmitter()` style.
```typescript
const fixture = magic.fixture(MyComponent);
const countChanged$ = magic.outputObserver(fixture.componentInstance.countChanged);
fixture.componentInstance.countChanged.emit(5);
expect(countChanged$.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith(5);
expect(countChanged$.latest).toBe(5);
```
---
## SpyObserver\<T\>
Returned by `magic.observer()`. Wraps an observable with Jasmine spies.
| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `next` | `jasmine.Spy` | Called on each emission |
| `error` | `jasmine.Spy` | Called on error |
| `complete` | `jasmine.Spy` | Called on completion |
| `observations` | `T[]` | Array of all emitted values |
| `latest` | `T` | Most recently emitted value |
---
## Common Anti-Patterns
### Do not use `injection()` for your mocks because then you need to cast back to SpyObj<T> or to the Mock class
### Do not create manual spies
`objectMock` and `serviceMock` auto-spy all prototype methods. Manual `jasmine.createSpy()` is unnecessary.
```typescript
// Bad
const mock = { doWork: jasmine.createSpy('doWork') };
// Good
const mock = magic.objectMock(MyClass, {});
mock.doWork.and.returnValue('result');
```
### Do not mock methods the test doesn't use
Only provide a property in the mock when you need a specific return value. Auto-spied methods return `undefined` by default, which is sufficient for unused code paths.
---
## Standalone Functions
**`observe<T>(observable$, name?)`**
Standalone alternative to `magic.observer()`. Use when you don't have (or need) an `NgMagicSetupTestBed` instance.
```typescript
import { observe } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
const spy = observe(myService.events$, 'events');
expect(spy.next).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expectedValue);
```
**`mock<S>(spySource?, mock?, dontSpy?)`**
Standalone alternative to `magic.objectMock()`. Creates a mock object from a class prototype without TestBed registration.
```typescript
import { mock } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
const myMock = mock(MyService, { getData: () => [] });
// myMock has spies for all MyService methods; getData calls through to the provided fn
```
**`spyOnFunctionsOf(target, source?)`**
Converts all methods of `target` into Jasmine spies in place. Inherited methods are overwritten on the object itself (not on the prototype) to avoid side effects. An optional `source` can add extra spies from another class's prototype.
```typescript
import { spyOnFunctionsOf } from '@peejay-solutions/ng-magic-test-bed';
const instance = spyOnFunctionsOf(new MyService());
instance.doSomething('x');
expect(instance.doSomething).toHaveBeenCalledWith('x');
// Use when creating non-TestBed instances that still need spy tracking
const factoryMock = spyOnFunctionsOf(new MyFactory());
const serviceMock = spyOnFunctionsOf(new MyHelperService());
const sut = new MyService(factoryMock, serviceMock);
```
---
## IFactory Interface
Used by `factoryMock`. Any service with a `create(...args): I` method qualifies.
```typescript
interface IFactory<I> {
  create(...args: any[]): I;
}
```
